For my mother's birthday, she gave our whole family, my sisters and mine, a truly special gift: a cruise along the beautiful Drina River, which forms the natural border between Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

![3791.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJW95kYkNVxYYgzD7VKUVFKNy2Z2ohuQm5dsuEmm2LSGxfMY2XRDQ5DKVNKTt9uHgZ.jpg)

We spent several wonderful days on Tara National Park, surrounded by forests, fresh mountain air, and breathtaking viewpoints. Our Drina cruise started at the stunning and calm Perućac Lake.

![3591.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqYrmQ4dsgb6euCTvdC7SfQ37THeVMQdrKRff3KnZBqVEp6JhX37JK7EoKH6ZmmfPjP.jpg)

![3588.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep7t5Q8RYC67jw7KvLEwY75wws7FmdDpVLPNyrm739ZK6HQXTjEc8jKguKzJA3MWfvF.jpg)

![3592.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EnWG8nSFwqbbzggLLCGwukQQu6yGGYGYctqeSQAF6T1ibx1QFDmyRBA2e7CLfpuxZap.jpg)

![3589.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3cLjT5UKrFRJn9xynrjUtBkTZ62CuNjHVVtoLXRpnWvt3tAft5LQSYhfuczfHYnWd.jpg)

From the lake, we boarded a charming boat called Grizzly and took our seats on the upper deck, ready to enjoy the scenery.

![3617.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqL5tcHxyycdzhtL4UBi2UFZAVk7qqakhfU8idNUs2PZnkztnbhFkxx6gUctoMYG7pX.jpg)

![3595.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpnALam6ptQBmcDF3qTNmgP4cu8CyUPtsyfVvAu6hejnmvQnZrLpf9yhhZkf4fbiw3Y.jpg)

![3601.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQtPq86EvjqHxQy4am8iXChMCAg4njJqoZPSRs9KG2XieqdpSG8NkdqyTdBg4zSdJs.jpg)

![3710.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqDiZuYC73uRY249UozN9cddGeaGyVggxCeqToFvjrJcfAZkQfuUrnMWUcaE6Ph8eqB.jpg)

As we set off, we were immediately captivated by the emerald-green river winding through dramatic cliffs and dense forests.

![3699.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EppHjoBRXLC9ekqgKv4cG9ttG9sAAek939E63ibMwcJdPZWR1kPNv8xRh7iPeiHm2BD.jpg)

![3719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJX7dG23RbeyN9GGwndCxsXTkRgXxv3uT2uogrGJ4xbP2wH27M3wPyedd639junxcs.jpg)

![3712.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EokbjMoCuvxaatpQPkr9RsbcwPEGjdSaaDBRqMtcsj94aLMHxE9z5rJvPTQRZdACcji.jpg)

![3729.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoEpY1yiWjJpNSVxnk8UdC61LLRCxAfpjRyHqGf9uQj8pqrE15ugx2C2qYvgdFp1sUH.jpg)

Trees seemed to grow straight out of the rocks.

![3723.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQutKMDCHdBs6Z88kSCGjKfdv11iFscsQga2g83uz2XtMZppLBJDiPoKzWurG16YRr.jpg)

![3724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpnBtFkRV2jVHZUZuT28DSj1HCmKTxFtr28j6daJpng9yPZ6HHwKuhXku5AhphcxmCp.jpg)

![3803.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo8SPFxo55ji8wdTW7rsV6R3TMM4AqKbGp28DZVxSE5bVpzTKznovT8cv7dHi9T2Azn.jpg)

And wooden cottages and small riverside camps added a sense of warmth and tranquility.

![3806.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoprzwE4eF3BVmBFHAveH9a7hMG1cngmEJMfooej651yeebZUv5WNxjBZnCtb5KUCEH.jpg)

![3810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGwxJshKNjNXtsfs9H4KG3sSXVqHWQY25K5JY8HWsvqcAxpSf5KrTS2mrUqsSik5sQ.jpg)

![3858.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eq9SviBhJqEoBaHAbRNTUm9UwM1hgr7ePLdyfxJ5TA7w8DgoBEQJHcgeR6cxkNLDx1x.jpg)

![3861.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJXAomGkD5LjwGvtNqhNHMFj1krCAGFRJRLxcHwaHpFdaQzaP3X7n3Jdf7b54wfnb1.jpg)

![3799.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQvGvFgSyW2em6o3ZL2mAhofQmqiz4qRE8NfUxqdx2Q1UHuayve6YCEC4z93DbdFVe.jpg)

![3883.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCh5ZHz9BAEM3WzQm93qKLKTGBwxa5wuRYi5MreoAwT3jFoXTrJnVWVKxYATpYUA3b.jpg)

During the cruise, our guide shared fascinating stories about the places we passed. He even told us to pay close attention, because on the way back there would be a quiz to test what we had learned.

![4010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EppHKmDa5p719X2tGV8Qb6fUdVLVY1nCRH9mitq68aLohPQEGEijYgHfJKiBQ6vfGEt.jpg)

![4009.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogMP4EZ74p4hFRti48EeZhyKSwdSLRjYUtNos7ePhSZyKVoKCnhX6AYmZUaKAuNr2U.jpg)

For about three hours, we sailed between Serbia and Bosnia, following the majestic Drina River towards Višegrad, the town closely associated with the Nobel Prize-winning writer Ivo Andrić. Along the way, we passed a very impressive monument: an old ship raised in memory of those who lost their lives during World War II.

![3873.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpnBKBA8sYAT28znAyABzKSFhjf3yBqMtjfYvWVe1GZzHJQqpth9YkjPrnpmfyAsZ97.jpg)

![3876.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo8SH8oQ4Nwj2CDV2qjZ7VVZZ7SgKxNdFigw4i2HNGiwSYD72dUzBRyWac2nPVDFx1z.jpg)

![3881.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGxUCwDtRYxQwmsuaqY1qDsSjpDaJ4x2VHUTst1ugLqNP7EeGFaCiYxGeAKsYDL61P.jpg)

My children especially loved exploring the lower deck, where some of our most exciting moments happened as we passed through the narrowest part of the canyon.

![3657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xyR81DwHnkMjcixRX8YPgYacgddxVjz1VXegCJDuMuYkHDMfTHem4ss5UH9rKs3V4ER.jpg)

![3690.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoniyvvYHeh6Wmv4pd3DjbBWdDaDrr5sqzNmyASZGHQTHHvhu7G5FcojfG6oQVCwD1g.jpg)

![3787.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xyQv1mEwEZvkkpc5nPvUaUeuF1Hb59VgbdX21FBxtzWCspkxUJjuQEe4tyn7dh8tbEJ.jpg)

After three unforgettable hours, we arrived in Višegrad. And that memorable stop deserves a story of its own in my next post.

![3745.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xKqyh8ew3HcTPjT5X4z3JSBhHmTtWfg5H75fmMfR8GHA9TBgypB9EbJXNCc1wiSaYmA.jpg)

Thank you for reading.

Jelena

![Brown and Beige Vintage Travel Plan Presentation.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/23vsE9VimAbXGwJmEiVKgdNGAdPGWg1yRmKUaHkgc5LSaAF6hX9N7h7VqMPjUn6ub5Zjt.jpg)
Desde el año pasado comencé con mis amigas a organizar salidas mensuales y uno de estos planes que surgieron fue este, ir a ver las estrellas. Ninguna demuestra un interés profundo por la astronomía, pero era un plan diferente que se adaptaba muy bien al presupuesto así que terminamos yendo a nuestro primer camping para ver las estrellas.

Last year, my friends and I started organizing monthly outings, and one of the ideas that came up was this: going stargazing. None of us are particularly interested in astronomy, but it was a unique activity that fit our budget perfectly, so we ended up going on our first camping trip to stargaze.
---
![mochilla y botas.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoEiLVzM9fsdk8ktNVDwhPPpNjyUcnoGdXgtnFwEHfVbQz3AVfxomYMNctWgD9EzUdx.png)
---

Listas para ver los objetos de Messier
Lists for observing Messier objects

Como todos los viajes aquí en la ciudad nos enteramos por Instagram, un grupo de personas que se dedican a observar los astros estaban ofertando esta ruta para para una noche acampando con la finalidad de observar los más de cien objetos que catalogo en su momento el astrónomo Charles Messier.

Since we find out about all the events here in town through Instagram, we learned that a group of stargazers was offering this trip—a one-night camping trip—to observe the more than 100 objects originally cataloged by the astronomer Charles Messier.
![1000330906.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoEoeEAXMn6ys81PXoFDZbiizjAJdXT24wZHoUtbbgyViz6GkvgcivnRioX3jMF3W9b.jpg)
![1000330889.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoeDsjisJFwfm9JEWw4stkBRsZL7EhxHYP8bRgA3kXBEyZ5ZYFDb7ndYBUDb8k7SA6L.jpg)
---
Que vamos, que yo en un principio no tenía ni idea de lo que estaban hablando con esto del Maraton Messier, más adelante, nos explicaron bien de que se trataba. Una vez hecho el contacto del viaje al que básicamente confirmamos asistencia un día antes, nos pidieron como requisito para vivir de mejor forma la experiencia del campamento descargar la App Stellarium que funciona como una guía para ayudarte a ubicar y reconocer cada punto que ves en el cielo.

To be honest, at first I had no idea what they were talking about with this “Messier Marathon,” but later on, they explained it all to us clearly. Once we'd made the arrangements for the trip—which we basically confirmed our attendance for the day before—they asked us, as a requirement to get the most out of the camp experience, to download the Stellarium app, which serves as a guide to help you locate and identify every object you see in the sky.
![1000330921.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EpVAapSLtogF1gHWXpnXR9jcRtioYj1ag38d5FXwuv87LMps1yx5qZuMWdBaHvMhF1Z.jpg)
El campamento sería en un lugar llamado Padre Diego, del estado Lara, Venezuela. Allí se ubica la caseta de los guardaparques del Parque Nacional Cerro Saroche.

The camp would be located in a place called Padre Diego, in the state of Lara, Venezuela. That is where the park rangers' station for Cerro Saroche National Park is located.
![1000330929.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EpNnRJpZMUyY2ZRin2xQQxkcQqu4Sw2AGL25jKbcqPUVHRo8e5kvhbTbWBtk7TuuPp5.jpg)
![1000330930.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EpzxhsdWNWNvorBqeti3jaxVmmhTjdnyBcgZfgkmnHZwk6Yax9iZ6ZwLrWbLkdCHT89.jpg)
---
Llegamos a eso de las 6 de la tarde y lo primero fue comenzar a armar las carpas, en nuestro caso decidimos optar por alquilar una a los organizadores del viaje en 5 USD, para mi sorpresa es un tipo de carpa que se arma casi como abrir un paraguas, super fácil y rápido.

We arrived around 6 p.m., and the first thing we did was start setting up the tents. In our case, we decided to rent one from the trip organizers for $5. To my surprise, it’s the kind of tent that sets up almost like opening an umbrella—super easy and quick.
![1000330941.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoyP16ANUwj83djaSUwMP7LRsyymWYWEQJWJAhmgxZZj1Utrm96R3Q6cjdnPvQoPjiM.jpg) ![1000330942.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Eoryt6WaEqGbBHSF3GUhGLefb4Q7DcXH9mN42iZV913t3QkZPnkuPFir3bd5gkr5RfR.jpg)
La siguiente actividad estaba guiada por los guardaparques y consistía en hacer el sendero de interpretación Cardenalito Larense que tienen en el parque.

The next activity was led by the park rangers and involved walking the Cardenalito Larense interpretive trail in the park.
![1000330964.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EqL6pLGQYJcVEXQ1BenuJP2ZvTuLYcz1iMR4EV6z6UJzCTgXsbCR7B2RniqiRLkuTFn.jpg)
![1000330972.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Ep3dsGtsBwsU9taji6WFL6HofmLGRhHPrEqt73ASZoPunNFcJLzudyp58PACPdybFz6.jpg)
---
En el sendero nos encontramos 7 estaciones donde vamos a ir viendo los tipos de vegetación, en especial en una zona xerófila. Entre todas las cosas que nos hablaron una curiosa es el nombre de Saroche que viene de la lengua indígena gayona y significa "refugio en el cerro."

Along the trail, we’ll come across seven stations where we’ll observe different types of vegetation, particularly in a xerophytic zone. Among all the things we were told, one interesting fact is the name “Saroche,” which comes from the Gayona indigenous language and means “refuge on the hill.”
![1000330975.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EpQuuJ7K1GrofyCUVcRJqmYW6onQvJ7ps5XFZvk6nyZzPxdgBueV5KaAMtM2PizYouX.jpg)
![1000330978.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Eq7MSUByKst597YL2o3ejzpRTvW8GrfsBraDXZ3Xu4ehjQmGzQJ3zANn93Qvr7VrzGJ.jpg)
---
Aqui te dejo algunas de las plantas que vimos allí.

Here are some of the plants we saw there.
![1000330958.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EpzxhsnGEH6jaVcCX2JDMH3wXEA3GurWKqXC5tU63jvkmBWW25vvsMjrbQw1sQ7Hb3y.jpg) *Yabo en floración* ![1000330980.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EorzQ2RYN4syVxXreYLdXJMk1ED9285JuwEvPTNsUck8Mw6jR6bJFkRARrFcnuJ5FZE.jpg) *Kalanchoe* ![1000330991.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoyR23HjMB71Ju2cthhFUneBLGRwxgPHBU62dzW2DTM2xABgREoXU5jNrqG7wW3H5W2.jpg) *Tillandsia o gallito* ![1000330994.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EqFpY6iUNMSvy1qWjHAJLpjuUfd3Qc8kgC1nbEH2q1BcPdx4bYTHKJy3Eq3qLdu3o58.jpg) *Cocuiza*
Este recorrido duro aproximadamente unos treinta minutos por lo que cuando salimos ya el sol se despedía de nosotras regalándonos este hermoso atardecer.

The walk took about thirty minutes, so by the time we left, the sun was already setting, treating us to this beautiful sunset.
![noche2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Ep1V4K4HDZiZm3usKuuArwXnjYiiMtJWuJjDhsymvfwVAZBH8oFem6Pag18TFMuKn9o.jpg)
Y con la puesta de sol comenzaba nuestra tarea de observación, aquí lo primero que se deja ver es el planeta Venus, pero disculpa lo borroso, mi zoom no dio para más.

And as the sun set, our stargazing began. The first thing you see here is the planet Venus, but please excuse the blurriness—my zoom just couldn't get any closer.
![1000331024.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoATujLovU2EGqp7JbF4PrrYvpqzFkUq4LVAsrriuxM8JG8JMeBD99FdqBQ1vkMWzLh.jpg)
Nos dieron una clase para explicarnos todo al respecto del Maratón Messier y cómo usar la App de Stellarium para reconocer lo que veíamos en el cielo, además de ello, también nos mostraron lo que es un planisferio celeste que es una herramienta que te ayuda también a ubicar que objeto astronómico vas a ver en qué lugar y a qué hora.

They gave us a lesson to explain everything about the Messier Marathon and how to use the Stellarium app to identify what we were seeing in the sky. In addition, they also showed us what a star chart is—a tool that helps you locate which astronomical objects you’ll be able to see, where, and at what time.
![1000331037.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Ep3cqz3jsBPcBHx9kmJM69qqBWnRqWeSY7p8XxeCUrsE3SZT4Q724b89RK362PhcqYg.jpg)
![1000331045.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Eoc67MhqJGfCArPq2HH1gRTqnbFo4sBBqZPxJYCUpE9hJP17qAE9i5rbQ9sZ4VfHnSR.jpg)
---
En este punto estábamos preocupados porque el cielo desde que llegamos estuvo muy nublado y nada que se despejaba. De todas formas, también estábamos preparados con los telescopios armados para en el primer momento de claridad salir corriendo a observar.

At that point, we were worried because the sky had been very cloudy ever since we arrived, and it didn't look like it was going to clear up. In any case, we were ready to go—with our telescopes set up—so that the moment the sky cleared, we could rush out to observe.
![1000331031.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Eo6CFSknHpVryQRKuiLZkoKdw4x68WnbrewPcTWEhV3F6GBFzBCERZNtZVWS1bTDVEJ.jpg)
![35ba4fe7-c5fd-4eda-87d9-0605828fc2ba.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoCasUAZCHNPeR676eHWqD6rLtPY8nxmVj3Tw7yKgBNbEbrfhHFjEgUgUNHMG7iUqrK.jpg)
---
Lo siguiente que vimos fue al planeta Jupiter y aquí se puso increíble todo, no podía creer lo cerca que se podía ver ese gran planeta. A eso de las 10 de la noche estábamos cenando y nos la pasábamos entre la carpa y saliendo y entrando observando las nubes en el cielo.

The next thing we saw was Jupiter, and that’s when everything became truly amazing—I couldn’t believe how close that huge planet looked. Around 10 p.m., we were having dinner and kept going back and forth between the tent and the outside, watching the clouds in the sky.
![1000331048.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoEhJ5c34ou2djRzUFSKxLK4d6Y8Q4VKui27EB5rjKU5hsi4v75Bh83gfVbGbn97fBE.jpg) ![1000331055.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Ep3dR5vTQXXF6TWfkcKc7wmwVd8RmnBCKuavKuUAtCReuYRofnxTW2KMBmxMeXNAjMD.jpg)
Bien entrada la madrugada comenzamos a ver constelaciones como la de Géminis, la Canis Mayor que tiene una estrella llamada Sirio que destaca bastante, también vimos a Orion, la estrella del norte, la constelación de la Osa Mayor y muchas otras más.

Well into the early hours of the morning, we began to see constellations such as Gemini and Canis Major, which contains a star called Sirius that really stands out. We also saw Orion, the North Star, the constellation Ursa Major, and many others.
![1000331069.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Eo8KZ418qBEbJpdKL8hmZAE3DbJfxenf1wPA4MZrjHeKANWCiC45q54PLA5s7LkyP2L.jpg)
Esta noche estuve despierta hasta eso de las 3 de la madrugada y de todo lo que vi esa noche lo que más me sorprendió fue ver el planeta Júpiter. Tenían un telescopio de mayor alcance y se allí se podía ver con claridad el planeta más dos de sus lunas, fue lo más increíble. Por supuesto que con un teléfono común y corriente no podía capturar fotos de estos objetos astronómicos.

Last night I stayed up until around 3 a.m., and of everything I saw that night, what surprised me most was seeing the planet Jupiter. They had a high-powered telescope, and through it you could clearly see the planet and two of its moons—it was absolutely incredible. Of course, with a regular cell phone, I couldn’t take any photos of these astronomical objects.
![cruz.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EoATvVPeK1geX1NnrtDZNBBYHNXQFVHukg6HHfHFt9gmTJidR8hdxTmTt12NnHEi7t6.jpg)
![1000331096.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EokbjFcKz6EA2yu4XCpxYH1AqYpG9CpbrHkiSq7g5iE7Q92t99NUsHF4e9QA5fuReMw.jpg)
![1000331097.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/Eq7LRBnahgZnuTvMLvfJesj5wZX2BTHjnMpriohoYySuEt6gph5sisPYR9KsFETHHFv.jpg)
---
La mañana comenzó desde bien temprano, pasa que cuando estamos en un lugar tan alejado de la ciudad puedes escuchar con mayor intensidad el canto de los pajaritos, funciona como una alarma, pero una alarma agradable de escuchar.

The morning started very early; when you're in a place so far from the city, you can hear the birds singing much more clearly—it's like an alarm clock, but a pleasant one to listen to.
![1000331090.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/23zGafjAUdQS4cHoQzQTFuYCJeczsvesGeKQbEzuf6Dev18gmhqCgohSEJz7JhRcbXoA2.jpg)
---
![botas.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arteyviajes/EpCFmnfQJRzm5S8fHCgkhepusrZy5N2mnZQUYWf6YdHyNxRMT6ooKQSF6ZNV4bZLr6t.jpg)
---
La verdad que iba con cero expectativas de la actividad y de hecho pospuse mucho la decisión de ir o no, pero ahora que lo hice te recomiendo con toda seguridad participar en una actividad como esta. Estas aprendiendo y maravillándote con todo lo que hay mas allá de lo que nos permiten ver nuestros ojos. Una cosa más, si te interesan las constelaciones descarga la App de Stellarium en tu teléfono, es muy sencilla de usar y la verdad puedes entretenerte bastante cualquier noche observando el cielo.

To be honest, I went into the activity with zero expectations, and I actually put off deciding whether or not to go for a long time. But now that I’ve done it, I can wholeheartedly recommend participating in an activity like this. You’ll learn and be amazed by everything that lies beyond what our eyes can see. One more thing: if you’re interested in constellations, download the Stellarium app on your phone—it’s very easy to use, and honestly, you can have a lot of fun any night just by looking up at the sky.

result.body: On the third day of my mini-vacation, I met up with my Taiwanese student. I've known him for quite a long time, too, but it's the first time we're meeting up in person. He came to Cebu with his mom, aunt, and cousin... and they invited me to go with them to Cebu Safari. I had to wake up early because the vehicle they chartered would arrive at their hotel at around 8:30 AM, and it takes me around an hour to get there from my cousin's place. I arrived there around 7:50 AM and waited for them in the lobby. The vehicle arrived earlier, at around 8:10 AM, so we headed to our destination ahead of schedule. It took us around 2 hours to get to the destination from their hotel, which was located in the downtown area of Cebu. It was pretty sunny, but the area is in the mountains, so it was windy and comfortable. It's pretty similar to where I live. Before entering, we took a photo at the entrance near the parking area. From here, we're going to ride a tram which will take us to the base camp. The base camp is basically the receiving area for guests. There's also a restaurant where people can enjoy some Filipino food. We were also given further instructions on how to explore the place. The first area we visited was the aviary dome, which was just beside the base camp. There were several species of birds, and guests can feed them for an extra price. I relayed the information given to us by the guides, so we tried to plan our route around the safari. The whole area is walkable, but there are tram stops where we can ride to certain points of the safari. Since we wanted to explore and enjoy the place, we decided to walk and follow the animal trail next to the safari fountain. I've always been fascinated by capybara. I've never seen it in person, but I had an image that they're pretty chill animals. I got more interested in them after knowing Raijinmaru from the anime World Trigger. *hahaha* I was so happy to finally see them. They're so cute!! They shared the same open space with the llamas and some other animals. The llama and capybara were casually chilling and taking a bath together. *haha* We saw more animals, but I was too distracted to take more photos. XD Then, we went to see the tigers. They had a tiger feeding at around 10:30 AM, but we were not able to arrive on time for it. Still, we were able to see this magnificent animal. Its enclosure is pretty wide, so we're lucky it stayed near the glass. The other one was quite far, but we saw it when we were walking towards another area. The safari also has its own veterinary medical center. We saw eggs being incubated and really young animals being taken care of before being released. We saw a lot of peacocks and other animals casually crossing the roads, or just chilling by the pathway. It's great to see that even though the place is technically a zoo, they're able to roam around a wide space. After visiting several more areas like the deer district, orangutown, and the safari stadium, we decided to take the tram and head to the white lion safari, which is among the farthest areas. There are three white lions in this area: Jack, Max, and Bugoy. It was interesting for me because our Golden Retriever's name is also Max... and they're of similar color. And from there, we visited the Dromedary Camels and Birds of the World areas. Then, we rode another tram going to the African Savanna. Before we entered the African Savanna, we checked out some otters, crocodiles, and turtles along the way. I used to live near a Crocodile farm, so it was interesting to see them in a different place. *haha* We had to ride another tram to go around the African Savanna. Luckily, I sat at the far end, so it was easy to see the animals. There were different types of animals, including impala, gazelle, waterbuck, zebras, and so on. We could go around the area for around 10 minutes, as the guide gave us more information about the animals. To be honest, I can't distinguish many of them as I'm not familiar with them... well, aside from the zebras. XD From there, we decided to walk again and explore other areas. The cheetah was resting. I remember my student's cousin typed in her phone's translator and told me the cheetah was quite chubby. *Hahah* We communicated with each other via a translation app since she couldn't speak English, but she wanted to talk with me. The view we see as we walk around is so pretty. There were a lot of trees and amazing green spaces. My student's mom and aunt were also fascinated by the plants, especially the wild orchids. My student told me that his aunt is a farmer, and they export flowers to Japan. That's why she's also very enthusiastic to explore the plants in the area. After more walking, we decided to finally have lunch. It was already around 2 PM at that time, but I thought it was a good thing because we were able to avoid the busy time. There were several places to eat, but the base camp and the outpost offered lunch. The others were mainly just drinks and snacks. We decided to eat at the outpost area, overlooking the giraffes. After our late lunch, we decided to head back to the base camp via the Canopy trail. It was the last area we had yet to explore. There were various animals, too... However, I only took photos of the pelicans because they were so interesting. XD We were able to explore almost the entire area except for the adventure rides and other facilities. We also skipped the garden and pavilion area, but we were able to see them while we were on the tram on our way back to the parking area. We dropped by the gift shop to check what was there before heading back to the city. We walked a lot, but it wasn't tiring because we could enjoy watching the animals. The animals didn't seem like they were in an enclosure *(well, except for the birds)*, because the area is too spacious. Some of them were even walking around from one place to another. I couldn't take photos of all the animals because I was trying to enjoy the moment. Though I took photos of the ones that really caught my attention. I also wanted to show the photos to my cousins. *haha* It would be awesome to go there again, but with my family next time. I had an enjoyable time with my student and his family, though. They were so kind and fun to be with despite the language barrier. They invited me to dinner as well, so I took them to a local area to eat some grilled food. They had fun eating using their hands and trying new things the Filipino way. I had a great time, and I gained a new friend... My student's cousin also loves reading manga and Webtoon, so we exchanged LINE and became chatmates. *hahaha* We came for the animals, but we found friendship. *LOL* Anyway, I'll end this post here. It's already midnight, so I'll go to bed soon. Thanks for reading, and see you around! I have been walking around my neightborhood for a long time, but there are still places nearby that I have not visited and fully explored. 

The marina in Gouves, right on the northern coast of my island, Crete - is one of those places.

This beautiful, seaside village is well known for its relaxed atmosphere, long beachfront, traditional tavernas, and easy access to many attractions. It has Pano (Upper Side) and Kato (Seafront side) Gouves, which is a more touristic places. Here,  visitors can enjoy both tranquility and convenience, as it is also full of tavernas, restaurants, hotels, organized beaches and also shops. 

In this post, we will explore its small but really nice and well taken care - Marina port.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZXVuwaLMUL17vTHHTEfouVWDCH5a7GpXThtVyq2pELLD/image.png)

The port was constructed in 2023, as the sign suggests and below you will find the website with more information. 
![IMG_0989.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUJqFNGvipqo8mu7RiMr1m2gkQzsSEjJJqTHDySQqh5ET/IMG_0989.jpeg)
http://www.portogouves.gr 

Gouves Port is a small harbor mainly used by local fishermen, small boats and sailing boats. Unlike the large commercial ports found in bigger cities, this harbor keeps a calm and authentic character. Here, you can watch fishing boats gently moving with the waves, see the two light houses, enjoy the sea breeze, come here for a lovely sunset spot (with some cat company sometimes) or simply sit nearby and admire the endless blue of the Cretan Sea.


![IMG_0984.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXyoM8JuUxNntWXWhRGF4EjJ2uNjq83fcZ83Gqix7VXSZ/IMG_0984.jpeg)|![IMG_0986.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUFzchCJScM9m9J2AFcCqQCnvz8JDnbtnkNuuh38daxc6/IMG_0986.jpeg)
-|-

The atmosphere changes throughout the day. In the morning, the area feels peaceful and fresh, while during sunset the harbor becomes especially beautiful as the golden light reflects on the water and the boats.


![IMG_0982.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYv357gchUJjzYRxckju7Ueq5iHCGAxXp84frEdwTLnu5/IMG_0982.jpeg)


The promenade around the port is ideal for a relaxing walk, photography, or simply enjoying a quiet moment away from crowded tourist areas.

Right next to the port, there are beach volley spots, sun loungers and beach chairs, as well as a sandy beach

https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ARsXmsfaA9Y

If you are lucky, you may find other visitors at the place too!
I found a super cute cat there, I think he was trying to fish - but I had no treats so he did not come near me :( 

https://youtube.com/shorts/qc2Xg9_9IIY?si=pilQdKomV9VbEXxS

He is super cute though, right?


![IMG_0985.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYkEVm2gUG1Vu1dCnR97vMUhuXPFxom1WDDK8Jbz2QH76/IMG_0985.jpeg)

At the port, there are two lighthouses, one black and white and one red and white.
They are the stars of the port, and I will try to take nights photo too! 

Here, you see the view from the end of the port .. and to the other smaller port that you will see right after the video

https://youtube.com/shorts/hC_aqTJqe7s?si=HpctU-nNf33cp1hQ

Right a few meters away, you will see another small beach, that is never windy.
It is next to a hotel, and there are just a couple of little boats parked there.


![IMG_1024.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT8LQR2Woxc2NpALkpxrBGuffpZYGaVE11EmD5dNb5AwF/IMG_1024.jpeg)

For content creators and photographers, this little harbor offers wonderful opportunities for authentic seaside shots, especially during golden hour.


![IMG_1026.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma8tzmnBiTgQQvEGkzq8wMtgtEmVohrymmVShs83fctBX/IMG_1026.jpeg)

The day I visited, the atmosphere was a bit dusty, so it created a creamy sunset (If I may say that)


![IMG_1028.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWRw19YK3KGwgBsw9y1HeMnp9objH2VEWAXpF6wAbqd3r/IMG_1028.jpeg)


![IMG_1019.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPynuhD7Ap9BwyF5dsMbMn8R9vQRrj3b2w22yMnABjZUi/IMG_1019.jpeg)

As I was walking home, I could not help taking a few last shots 
(I wish they had their heads leaned together)

![IMG_1030.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcGsFbuR4u3HQQusdBUBPFxan2Tio4rAHpMRZWaHVi3w3/IMG_1030.jpeg)

And one of the last images was this one.
Family moments, at the sunset.

I always smile when I see that.. I hope I dont look creepy :) 


![IMG_1031.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXMKDT3riz1SCDPesATnxvqJSAvQLrTBAyzFR35uWsnn8/IMG_1031.jpeg)

Did you like my little port? 


More Gouves and a lovely little beach: https://worldmappin.com/@katerinaramm/discovery-of-a-little-beach-let-me-guide-you-there-gouves-crete

## English version
The Manzanares River is the most important freshwater waterway in Sucre State; it is approximately 81 kilometers long, which gives an idea of its magnitude. It originates in the imposing Cerro Turimiquire, flows through the city of Cumana, and empties into the Caribbean Sea via the Gulf of Cariaco.
![1000114753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23vsScYBFt6Qs2kjyAH8Xz4xrxycmvwDKYYSry2XPa6CKYcqws28nvHvp19v1Ej3LvVD2.jpg)
In the not-too-distant past, its waters were crystal clear along most of its course, but now, as a discharge point for sewage, pollution has wreaked havoc on the stretch that runs through Cumaná. Currently, its flow has decreased because the municipality is dredging it; following a major emergency in which the main transfer line of the system that supplies water to the city collapsed, the decision was made to use water from the Manzanares River, previously treated by water treatment plants.
![1000113765.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/242hWoddYLosK87ieLg1sJBH8o8qM2gVo2jeFumsbHNnq9JSf6inbUcTySRf7vThSiuPW.jpg)
![1000113773.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EowGdCYbDoY2ELjvTkhYgC5Q37fp4qGKN3gTveBQoPYLxcSPty1SdHoM8xyUXt2LoSf.jpg)
Once again, the importance of the Manzanares River to Cumana is evident; this waterway has inspired various artistic expressions such as songs, paintings, poems, and stories. Over the years, it has been a source of both joy and sorrow, which is why—and for many other reasons—it stands as a historical landmark. One of the most iconic songs is “River Manzanares” by José Antonio Lopez, which has become almost an anthem at the local level.
![1000113769.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eqd9u6iKv2GmqiqpBfj7cKmYHFjzRrMq2CW7V98ozgyMgCDZkibrLjsVR6zYtArPLhM.jpg)
![1000113766.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpQuuK2NLnE1KbLQV9hD5h6ZUtMGhraZuouYsYK6tvkGLL3Qx8MhZSmzkvHAwPPuZx3.jpg)
Although part of the river is still navigable, pollution levels have contributed to the decline in small boats; at least in Cumana, very few are now seen near the Market and the neighborhoods of La Trinidad and Las Palomas, through which the Manzanares flows until it reaches the river mouth, known as the city’s fishing pier.
![1000113754.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EppLeQCu5ZeMrPosnDekigJZK989HHhd7DKSCrVwsDJSWJAL38SjgvMsrYvW5ZTkrZx.jpg)
![1000113764.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Ep3errjoo1pZWAUtgxBPvo9p829nE82WA9meVP3Zuqp4aU4tqqoUL4PGsivXj84bE15.jpg)
This river has been a faithful witness to the past and to history; it was vital to the founding of Cumaná because it became the source of fresh water for the first settlers who established themselves in the San Francisco area, next to the Castle and the Basilica of Santa Inés. The old aqueduct was built from the Manzanares River and inaugurated in the early 1800s, serving as one of the foundations for development from the colonial era onward.
![1000113759.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EprTX2f3xrsUZneTTyioykYYW43N9vBTDkM833x8ujo6dPoGFGq2aR1HvmoNXT8Dagm.jpg)
![1000113762.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Epzy7o8wD89xcB82MjQJ6KJacJS6vGFxreaFwNFUAhSnnobsTiEUT1fgBRHQmEpzFc8.jpg)
The images I’m showing you today are from a walk through the city center, right across the bridge connecting Mariño Street with Ayacucho Square. The river can be seen from various parts of downtown, with Guaiqueri Park, the Gómez Rubio Bridge, the Guzman Blanco Bridge, and Petión Avenue being the best spots to view it as it winds through the city.
*** ***
## Versión en Español
El Río Manzanares es el caudal de agua dulce más importante del estado Sucre, posee aproximadamente 81 kilómetros de longitud, lo que concede una idea de su magnitud. Nace en el imponente Cerro Turimiquire, atraviesa la ciudad de Cumaná y desemboca en el Mar Caribe a través del Golfo de Cariaco.
![1000114753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23vsScYBFt6Qs2kjyAH8Xz4xrxycmvwDKYYSry2XPa6CKYcqws28nvHvp19v1Ej3LvVD2.jpg)
En tiempos algo remotos, era cristalino en la mayor parte de su recorrido, pero ahora, al ser desahogo de aguas servidas, la contaminación ha hecho estragos en el tramo que recorre Cumaná. Actualmente su caudal ha descendido debido a que la municipalidad lo está dragando ya que ante una gran contingencia, se derrumbó el eje transvase del sistema que surte de agua a la ciudad, se ha optado por utilizar el agua del Manzanares, previamente tratada por plantas de potabilización.
![1000113765.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/242hWoddYLosK87ieLg1sJBH8o8qM2gVo2jeFumsbHNnq9JSf6inbUcTySRf7vThSiuPW.jpg)
![1000113773.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EowGdCYbDoY2ELjvTkhYgC5Q37fp4qGKN3gTveBQoPYLxcSPty1SdHoM8xyUXt2LoSf.jpg)
De nuevo se demuestra la importancia del río Manzanares para Cumaná, caudal que ha sido inspiración para diversas manifestaciones artísticas tales como canciones, pinturas, poemas y narraciones. A lo largo de los años ha sido motivo de alegrías y tristezas, por eso y más es un referente histórico. Uno de los temas musicales más emblemáticos es "Río Manzanares" de José Antonio López, casi un himno a nivel local.
![1000113769.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eqd9u6iKv2GmqiqpBfj7cKmYHFjzRrMq2CW7V98ozgyMgCDZkibrLjsVR6zYtArPLhM.jpg)
![1000113766.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpQuuK2NLnE1KbLQV9hD5h6ZUtMGhraZuouYsYK6tvkGLL3Qx8MhZSmzkvHAwPPuZx3.jpg)
Si bien una parte del río todavía es navegable, el nivel de contaminación ha contribuido a que las pequeñas embarcaciones cada vez sean menos vistas, al menos en Cumaná son muy pocas las que se observan ahora cerca del Mercado y los barrios La Trinidad y Las Palomas, por donde el Manzanares tiene su paso hasta llegar a la Boca del río, conocido como el muelle pesquero de la ciudad.
![1000113754.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EppLeQCu5ZeMrPosnDekigJZK989HHhd7DKSCrVwsDJSWJAL38SjgvMsrYvW5ZTkrZx.jpg)
![1000113764.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Ep3errjoo1pZWAUtgxBPvo9p829nE82WA9meVP3Zuqp4aU4tqqoUL4PGsivXj84bE15.jpg)
Este río ha sido testigo fiel del pasado y de la historia, fue vital para la fundación de Cumaná porque llegó a ser la fuente de agua dulce para estos primeros pobladores que se instalaron en la zona de San Francisco, al lado del Castillo, y de la Basílica de Santa Inés. El acueducto viejo fue construido a partir del Manzanares e inaugurado a principios de 1800, una de las bases para el desarrollo a partir de la época colonial.
![1000113759.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EprTX2f3xrsUZneTTyioykYYW43N9vBTDkM833x8ujo6dPoGFGq2aR1HvmoNXT8Dagm.jpg)
![1000113762.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Epzy7o8wD89xcB82MjQJ6KJacJS6vGFxreaFwNFUAhSnnobsTiEUT1fgBRHQmEpzFc8.jpg)
Las imágenes que hoy les muestro son de una caminata por el centro de la ciudad, justo por el puente que comunica la calle Mariño con la Plaza Ayacucho. Desde varios sectores del centro se puede observar el río siendo el parque Guaiqueri, el puente Gómez Rubio, el puente Guzmán Blanco y la avenida Petión los puntos preferidos para contemplarlo en su recorrido por la ciudad.

ENGLISH VERSION (click here!) Hello, travelers. Happy Wednesday to everyone. During my visit to the state of Mérida, before heading to the little town of Tabay, we stopped by Juan’s Haunted House. I’d wanted to visit it for a long time, but hadn’t been able to until this trip, when I finally had the chance. This house is right next to El Viejo Molinero, which I showed you in my previous post. ![InShot_20260512_092216300.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU3Y9hxfRmFqy4zPtYBnJ1NZU4BoeX2ujCuJoY2H2c79T/InShot_20260512_092216300.jpg) Part of the story behind this place is that Juan wanted to get married, but to do so he had to build a house for his fiancée. He had no idea how to do it since he had never built one before. His father told him, “You should build it on flat ground, starting with the walls and finishing with the roof,” but since he was in such a hurry, he didn’t pay much attention to his father, and his house ended up with some flaws that have led people to call it today: Juan’s Haunted House. ![20260403_163658.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmewQixRjQEkxDcbkPB5AriuhSWgXyLqPqaaQGhS4U8xPx/20260403_163658.jpg) ![20260403_163526.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY9xxmddwMQtjxYF6jZpGkssZKcFgWaMXv6khmEQmPaWW/20260403_163526.jpg) ![20260403_161344.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTm2ntq5nVAi5cmFoSJy6cuAEeQoGvaKJaSByBAnzRsHZ/20260403_161344.jpg) As we entered the house, we walked through a dark hallway. I was holding Ricardo’s hand because I was scared, and we couldn’t use the light from our cell phones. As we walked, I had the feeling that something was hanging from the ceiling. ![20260403_161359.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU7b7LNizKs1Ep5m616bXU1ojfLucCEM2SnLVh96nqJf7/20260403_161359.jpg) That hallway led us straight to the first room, called the betting room, where the entire floor and the objects—or rather, the chairs—seemed to have a slight tilt. Juan invited his friends, who lost all their money trying to win, since there were several games where no one could win; among them were completing a lap around the circle by following the line and getting up from a chair, It became clear that none of those present could actually win; in fact, none of them could even get up from the chair. ![20260403_161933.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmf86wsP2gQJQYG4NSK3sdqXZXsBnpS5mfdZPkrnngByq5/20260403_161933.jpg) ![20260403_161937.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcuiRQ6APdHZn1XYzKrAkLTTihC4FDhZKFp6snoZmUqMz/20260403_161937.jpg) ![20260403_162227.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmabikJw2zbc1kosig6535X31kNYxoAeGJxmMKX11vegAQ/20260403_162227.jpg) ![20260403_162341.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVRVPZafJxdxHEp1DirgcuVxoZcqwG6ZUMP7upErCU77a/20260403_162341.jpg) Then we went to the game room, where there was a pool table that worked in reverse—I suppose because of the table’s slope. Now, what’s inexplicable is that there was a tube to dispense the balls, and instead of going down, they went up. ![20260403_162707.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcckctFtCKPDrHxFMZxaWUoyR2SVqZkPD1WdqZkesQWXs/20260403_162707.jpg) ![20260403_162714.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZtpnf88axiPxRqHdb5wQ3uU3tCqTgAFPRzeX2tg4T2gi/20260403_162714.jpg) ![20260403_162832.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQvycwdVfS628onHHMiVbBUzySTu7DAHkuz6gBZNh4cun/20260403_162832.jpg) In the bathroom, when they went to take a shower, no matter how much they stood under the showerhead, the water would run off to the side, which is why Juan ended up bathing with a plastic container so he could pour water over his body. ![20260403_162938.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc9zTt1wwuQoLtqCSAgYUGYyVdBQZ53Nfb8FtVm8UCd9E/20260403_162938.jpg) ![20260403_163037.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNjrFNA3yq1pgsUM4JBMLgQPEHjhTY5uUivHAdNNo61gY/20260403_163037.jpg) The last room we visited in the house was the kitchen, where they spent hours cooking because the fire wouldn’t stay in one place, and if they tried to roll out dough, the rolling pin would roll back up, making the task more difficult. ![20260403_163145.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNmLxGjQCnZHmkrv2cD7wqC75fz1JTRdWp8h8dDTwJjvb/20260403_163145.jpg) ![20260403_163220.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPn6Kv2JFtRncFWmctYh5AF3m3tWJ99yqbFjbtbycRHDR/20260403_163220.jpg) ![20260403_163234.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVKAB8YFK2hEAj2sNJHtdetKXnPsCqRQPsUbCwe7eEJUu/20260403_163234.jpg) We said goodbye to this place, and although I don’t really know exactly what goes on in this house, when I left I tried to explain the situations that occur there, and what I thought was that there’s a bit of physics in its inner magic. ![20260403_163310.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfQTybMEucHenZDhHapRX7PR7SkDU4v75KmGt6N43i9dC/20260403_163310.jpg) ![20260403_163425.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbUvaVaHkkEdryoMZ6jSpbiSdHW3qJ2fgz418NxkYuc3y/20260403_163425.jpg)

Hola, viajeros. Feliz miércoles para todos. En mi visita por el estado Mérida, antes de irnos al pueblito de Tabay llegamos a la Casa Encantada de Juan, desde hace mucho tiempo quería conocerla, pero no había podido hasta que en mi último viaje se presentó la grandiosa oportunidad de conocerla. Esta casa queda justo al lado de el Viejo Molinero que les mostraba en mi anterior publicación. ![InShot_20260512_092216300.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU3Y9hxfRmFqy4zPtYBnJ1NZU4BoeX2ujCuJoY2H2c79T/InShot_20260512_092216300.jpg) Un poco de la historia de este lugar esta basada en que Juan quería casarse pero para eso tenía que construirle una casa a su prometida, el no tenía idea de como hacerlo ya que nunca había construido una, su padre le dijo: "Que debía hacerlo sobre un terreno actualmente: La casa encantada de Juan. ![20260403_163658.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmewQixRjQEkxDcbkPB5AriuhSWgXyLqPqaaQGhS4U8xPx/20260403_163658.jpg) [source](https://x.com/SAgovnews/status/2054169724603572536) The unemployment rate in South Africa has been consistently above 30% for the last 5 years so adding an extra 1.2% for the first quarter of 2026 is hardly a shocker. It is the way this is reported that is hard to actually work out as they have a system that does not tell the entire truth so the 32.7% is a manipulated percentage that hides the real facts.
[source](https://x.com/FMFSouthAfrica/status/2054176918971334753/photo/1) There are so many official/unofficial stats the important part is not the exact number, but knowing these are increasing in a negative way. The recent tax report stated that only 10% of people working are paying taxes and the more people out of work creates more pressure to raise taxes on those working. How about using those taxes to create employment before there is no money left to create enough taxes to make this a possible solution? If no tax revenue is filtering back into the economy then the economy has no boost to get things working how they should. In my thought process if you do not have a job and are also of working age then you are unemployed, but the stats do not work that way. That would be too easy and would also show how bad the figures really are which is not good for the government.
[source](https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/860202/south-africas-unemployment-rate-gets-worse-as-over-300000-people-lose-their-jobs/) As you can see from the above the official labor force is 24.9 million which somehow does not include the other 17.3 million who are still of working age and unemployed. The official/unofficial total as no one knows the real figures of how many people reside in South Africa is a working population of 42.2 million with 16.8 million employed leaving 24.4 million unemployed. A simple calculation tells you that the unemployed rate is virtually smack bang on 60% which is nearly double the official unemployment rate. Imagine governing a country where 60% of the population has no work and no future prospects of finding work and justifying any form of corruption at the top. The money being stolen should be used on creating jobs and getting the economy moving through upgrading infrastructure and the likes. The BEE excuse of raising more capital by charging businesses 2% of net profit is a sham and is only making those at the top of the food chain richer and those at the bottom poorer. This is why keeping the mases uneducated works because they do not understand the game being played which is a game of screwing the masses for self enrichment. How refreshing it would be if corruption seized to exist and the population was put first like it should be. The economy would boom and everyone would be positively affected which is only a dream scenario as the government cannot see this as the only ones sacrificing would be them by not stealing. Finally the world has woken up to the fact that funding NGO's in African countries does not work as that money will be diluted by those in power and you have to be woke not to realise this. Without that free NGO money the problem is now they are having to get creative in other ways to steal.
[source](https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/860202/south-africas-unemployment-rate-gets-worse-as-over-300000-people-lose-their-jobs/) The stats are most likely far worse than the unofficial stats due to the way the stats are compiled. The government uses an external agency who uses a small settlement outside of Pretoria for their figures. They know if they ventured further a field like to the Eastern Cape these figures would show a very different reality and most likely would be the end of the ANC controlled government. Over 300K jobs lost in the community and social services sector is rather telling as the vast majority of households are deep in debt and with the increase in minimum wages back in March would have seen many jobs lost. The biggest red flag for myself is seeing 28K jobs lost in private households which would be gardeners and housekeepers known as domestic workers. These are generally unskilled workers on the lowest salaries and the bottom of the food chain. When households start cutting back to this extent that is a sign that things are rough in the economy and there will be more unemployment on the rise. Stats say there is roughly 1million employed in this sector and they will always be the first ones to be let go when the economy is struggling. The next quarter will be telling if this figure continues to rise which it should do as the economy is not improving plus extra fuel costs and inflation making more households cut back on expenses. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYLkwQHgJbDrUigXgwUXxaTZbZDz3fmUupfwFT8xdSRum/img_9586.png)
This is how the next chapter began... Así comenzó el siguiente capítulo…
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmePFqQwb5qXvTc31uNaxqdFpUrSETqHzUAPkbqhapkhEA/img_3438.jpg)
As I told you in the previous post, this day came full of emotions that I didn't know exactly how to explain. After that first approach to my roots, came something even more special: knowing part of my family that I had never seen. And it all started in Felton... with a dawn that already seemed to warn that this was not going to be just any day. > Tal como les adelanté en el post anterior este día venía cargado de emociones que no sabía exactamente cómo explicar. Después de ese primer acercamiento a mis raíces, venía algo aún más especial:conocer a parte de mi familia que nunca había visto. Y todo comenzó en Felton… con un amanecer que ya parecía avisar que este no iba a ser un día cualquiera.
Felton waking up between buildings and the sea. Felton despertando entre edificios y el mar.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdwbPvHz4pkZD3FGPt7EWbc8MkHTj5d4G2J7vy6vauMJX/img_3442.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQMqGisq593ekaVxNVgvyZBFFwpdV7cVNYP46gVA68tGN/img_3441.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZoNBuMGKtEhayRWqzcrrH3FGcFNvqFmHkB5uychQscvM/img_3444.jpg)
[//]:# (!pinmapple 20.73382 lat -75.59583 long d3scr) Walking around here is feeling a different rhythm with a characteristic landscape. On the coastal edge, mangrobe formations and other halophile plant communities are recorded; inland, shruff and anthropic pastures predominate. The pines that are seen are not a unique type "own" of the place, the pines there are rather sown by man. > Caminar por aquí es sentir un ritmo diferente con un paisaje característico. En el borde costero se registran formaciones de manglar y otras comunidades vegetales halófilas; tierra adentro predominan matorrales y pastizales antrópicos. Los pinos que se ven no son un tipo único “propio” del lugar, los pinos ahí son más bien sembrados por el hombre.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcbewk8pxrjYr3w9M4K5PXfBUjXg11Typcghyf9DMuEoR/img_3466.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbPm5ZQ498VaKFBoXJdZaFQXjx3iSh8XZM9WKTt7cMdme/img_3449.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbLqLwVWjjWsNnhcQMKTgnSs5fk7yt7aYJvbe31x6hhg7/img_3455.jpg)
Among the trees, what used to be a polyclinic, today almost hidden. Deteriorated by the passage of time and the abandonment of man. > Entre los árboles, lo que antes fue un policlínico, hoy casi escondido. Deteriorado por el paso del tiempo y el abandono del hombre.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT2gCv8fGwqVPQTFUgGTpbkHNJ1ayDf2Vn5nVWKVEKgQg/img_3461.jpg)
This place was the old social circle, where there was music, encounters and life. > Este lugar era el antiguo círculo social, donde había música, encuentros y vida.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU5cAZBgYqcCMjaQSVdZFK4NZF29t23Ncf7kdg6gqDMLA/img_3462.jpg)
Felton is not even half of what he came to do in his time, a place that before was full of people, of movement, of life... It went out and what hurts the most is that you can still feel the footprints. And in the midst of all that, one of the most important moments of the trip arrived. > Felton no es ni la mitad de lo que en su tiempo llego hacer, un lugar que antes estaban llenos de gente, de movimiento, de vida…Se apagó y lo que más duele es que todavía se sienten las huellas. Y en medio de todo eso, llegó uno de los momentos más importantes del viaje.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPU9ym5z5UnqjGKLMT3kdrDMs454cknNgzQQw6Ap7YRJM/img_3477.jpg)
Meeting my aunts for the first time, something I had been waiting for years. There was no distance. There was no discomfort. It was as if we already knew each other. As if time doesn't matter when there's something stronger that connects everything. But that day I still had something else saved. > Conocerlas por primera vez a mis tías, algo que llevaba años esperando. No hubo distancia. No hubo incomodidad. Fue como si ya nos conociéramos. Como si el tiempo no importara cuando hay algo más fuerte que lo conecta todo. Pero ese día todavía tenía guardado algo más.

Vuelta Larga Mayarí

It is a rural community belonging to the municipality of Mayarí, it is near Felton. Although it is not a tourist or famous place, Vuelta Larga is important because it represents the real life of many Cuban peoples, especially that of my father. > Es una comunidad rural perteneciente al municipio de Mayarí, está cerca de Felton. Aunque no es un lugar turístico ni famoso, Vuelta Larga es importante porque representa la vida real de muchos pueblos cubanos, en especial la de mi padre. [//]:# (!pinmapple 20.70338 lat -75.62335 long d3scr)
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdhVxyquGeHD832QeS2yNkCvhEru9YbXx75bNrLuzAGSu/img_3493.jpg)
On my tour I could see simple details, but that make the place even more special, the flowers and the elderberry (a fruit that my dad ate as a child, and that I was seeing for the first time). > En mi recorrido pude ver detalles simples, pero que hacen el lugar aún más especial, las flores y el Saúco(una fruta que mi papá comía de niño, y que yo estaba viendo por primera vez).
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX1FjJfz13jL7d1HDDSMxRVU8t3FEUGaP66SwkuVUSQVA/img_3497.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf7AZ7vSLW6JfX7meY4bS2VU1Rzuek9NNb6AGhsE948cp/img_3492.jpg)
This store was very famous in its time, one of those that keep stories. The store where they could go to get what they needed for the family and those in charge of going were the little ones, which for them was the most fun. > Esta tienda fue muy famosa en su tiempo, de esas que guardan historias. La tienda donde podían ir a buscar lo necesario para la familia y los encargados de ir eran los más pequeños, que para ellos eso era de lo más divertido.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQEJbaWWu3jvx1rh5q5Y6yqRw1u4EyPnh3QfafUmStqM4/img_3542.jpg)
This way you entered my dad's house. The house is no longer there. Nothing is left built. But even so, being there was enough. > Por aquí se entraba a la casa de mi papá. La casa ya no está. No queda nada construido. Pero aun así, estar ahí fue suficiente.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcM4SGuXQe25dVbuWocxpde68NU2KRPon8vPTk6vGwoBp/img_3494.jpg)
My cousin took me to see the Long Return Bridge. I really wanted to see it, I listened to my dad's stories and I was excited just thinking that such a structure was real. > Mi prima me llevo a ver el Puente de Vuelta Larga. Tenía muchas ganas de verlo, escuchaba las historias de mi papá y me emocionaba solo de pensar que semejante estructura fuera real.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXeRMKSR4Y34NLNrfkQbEyZx6jVfdiQRwuFNaoG6KzCG5/img_3501.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaf6st8yKC4G3nDTPNryRiCBgpxLqt2UsAUYXeSUDVTaF/img_9492.png)
This bridge has something that impresses since you see it. But from above it feels completely different. > Este puente tiene algo que impresiona desde que lo ves. Pero desde arriba se siente completamente diferente.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfZ1JnNsP9ozoPQMJSjDsZksC2RAvzo3CmkhubqfGDYNQ/img_9489.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRh2Xjx5FnK9KARGjcMWvuEX12JXgxdB3Gh39nUxHyLse/img_9486.png)
The rusty color indicates aged steel without recent maintenance. > El color oxidado indica acero envejecido sin mantenimiento reciente.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXEei2VT6UUGAWmJ37vycBQ3CARXY2EDdAys3p6ZFsb9Y/img_9491.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWxXQYPxvWFSvRXFvW5yfwPdW2TDMDFiA8QbRLbmg6Ntd/img_9481.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPz6Z4xrnKWKcoKMQTvL2ZnPYCgreHibeCiX9EdiX2Zzv/img_3506.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSwAb8HaAq5VsFbSXS2ya4ZWB6VMRzCYwaeWz9anQUEE8/img_9484.png)
Years ago, boats passed through here, the water is surprisingly deep. From above you can even see large fish, moving quietly in the water. > Hace años, por aquí pasaban barcos, el agua es sorprendentemente profunda. Desde arriba incluso se pueden ver peces grandes, moviéndose tranquilos en el agua.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbQzwhj6MUy3Dh6jrHFQFvtvorLTXp9jCRCEwmF1NEBsh/img_3539.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfP1aGPQGz4RPA9xGXZNpji178QJVAUhfoRWGrypdUgrA/img_9488.png)
But what marked me the most is being there... looking at him... walking him... it was like entering a part of his life that I had never lived. > Pero lo que más me marcó es estar ahí…mirarlo…caminarlo…fue como entrar en una parte de su vida que nunca había vivido yo.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbgotH6ShN6zai8EAE455zHUwGcRb9iVz1WrTBeSGwfcp/img_3535.jpg)
This day was undoubtedly one of the best. I didn't want to go, the heart is where the soul feels at peace and that feeling can't be explained. Have you ever been to a place that doesn't mean much to others, but to you is everything? > Este día sin duda fue de los mejores. No m quería ir, el corazón es de donde el alma se siente en paz y ese sentimiento no se puede explicar. ¿Alguna vez has estado en un lugar que no significa mucho para otros, pero para ti lo es todo? In the next post everything changes, less history, more nature, another rhythm. Thank you for joining me in this chapter, a very tight greeting!! En el próximo post todo cambia, menos historia, más naturaleza, otro ritmo. Gracias por acompañarme en este capítulo, un saludito bien apretado!! #Worldmappin #Travel #Cuba #Holguin #TravelStory #Roots #EmotionalTravel #CubanCulture #HiddenGems

#
[ENG]
Greetings, dear friends of Worldmappin, and welcome to my blog. Today I’m sharing an extraordinary photo gallery of urban art designed to revitalize the historic district of Cumaná, the capital of Sucre State, Venezuela. In addition to the area’s striking colonial architecture—thanks to its colorful houses, monuments, and narrow, cobblestone streets—to further revitalize the surrounding areas, they have created “Ciudad Mural,” a project that showcases open-air urban art.
From the moment you begin your stroll through the oldest part of the continent’s first city, you’ll see various artistic scenes in all their splendor. Each one represents the culture, traditions, coastal identity, heritage, nature, and traditional cuisine of the eastern region of Sucre State. The facades of the colonial houses became the perfect canvas for the artistic works of the City of Murals, though it wasn’t just the houses—businesses and even parking lots were also used. As we gather in the plaza where the Minor Basilica of Santa Inés is located, we find a painting honoring the Venezuelan writer and poet born in Manicuare, Cruz Salmerón Acosta.
![1772466310527.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZPTmUASxZNAp8xEEeiSGfknktS24TW9bM51oJxyvaDnA/1772466310527.jpg)
![1772466310468.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX8WhVae2a8jmoyBkaMRTvTXaLdgDAzvDWQP6Kmv5vujR/1772466310468.jpg)
In addition to depicting the renowned poet of martyrdom—also known as “The Loner of the Manicuare Summit”—this piece of urban art features a scene typical of the Araya Peninsula, such as the sea, seafood, and pelicans, which are part of the coast’s native wildlife. Cruz Salmerón Acosta is remembered for his poem “Azul,” and the mural features not only the drawing but also the first stanza of the poem, which is worth mentioning:
The blue of that distant peak toward which my thoughts fly under the blue peace of the morning, a color that reveals so much to me! [Source](https://www.poeticous.com/cruz-maria-salmeron-acosta/azul?locale=es)
Another figure that graces the City of Murals is the portrait of Leonor Guerra, created by the Cuban artist Ivette Dorticós; her signature indicates that this artwork is recent, dating from 2025. One fascinating aspect of this project is that every time you visit the historic district, you discover new works. Leonor de la Guerra was a native of Cumaná remembered for her courage in confronting the Spanish colonial authorities.
![1772466310566.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbvACbKNfsp5niDDZ8zRKYX6YjX5aUY78U7Rmm11hYnXW/1772466310566.jpg)
![1777736257636.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRPZJFRJUmJeqb2GpvqA6B3JDFVWFqGdLNp1t47zNFjBE/1777736257636.jpg)
![1772466310428.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQszvbFShpt11Z8LFAc9HQJoGAzT15ggecTezU72victc/1772466310428.jpg)
The city of Cumaná is a coastal area famous for its beaches and seafood cuisine; it is considered a land of grace. It is known as the “Firstborn of the American Continent” because it was founded by Spanish colonists, which is why its roots encompass a blend of races, traditions, and cultures. That is why, in the City of Murals, we find works that combine and highlight elements reflecting its indigenous and African roots, seascapes, typical coastal wildlife, folk music traditions, and cuisine, where the main traditional dish is fish.
The so-called “City of Murals” is beautiful and very colorful, not only because of the colonial-era architecture and facades adorned with street art, but also because of the many flower-filled plants, which attract tourists with their myriad hues. Another facade that represents the region’s identity features a portrait of an indigenous child, paying homage to the ancestral heritage and culture of Sucre State. On another facade, the artwork depicts the characteristic landscape of the coastal area, distinctive cuisine, local fruits, and a figure of a woman posing with a fish atop a two-headed turtle. This symbolizes the statue of the indigenous man, representing the Cumanés people, and at the same time, the warm welcome extended to tourists upon their arrival in the city. This statue was located at a roundabout where Arístides Rojas, Universidad, Arismendi, and Nueva Toledo avenues intersect. Currently, the statue is no longer there; it was moved to the entrance of Cumaná, specifically on Universidad Avenue in the Los Bordones neighborhood.
![1772466310606.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYWi7SZTB9yXvwuVCHiDb7EWX1LEzTFzkMDTduew5MQtA/1772466310606.jpg)
![1777736257560.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQaxjudFmWX2NnLiV4A9sf37ijNr6aCnm4u1rZMugj8aT/1777736257560.jpg)
![1777736257349.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNysGfRcMji32HppcVgxRCTJaF6XcDLaSxshyPKWTFGyV/1777736257349.jpg)
![1777736257688.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSA2nUXxjASfcHMeKnEKyx1MHf6boqEkkMZLoSATc4xR6/1777736257688.jpg)
The state of Sucre and the people of Cumaná are known for their joy, dancing, and music, which is why many notable figures hail from there, such as Mariano Ribera, Gualberto Ibarreto, and María Rodríguez, known as “La Sirena de Cumaná.” The latter was an important figure in music, well known for her dancing—which is why she was also known as La Mariposa bailadora de Cumaná—and was a Venezuelan singer and cultural figure. On the mural featuring the tribute portrait to the Siren of Cumaná, a few lines from the lyrics of the song “Ay Cumaná” have been inscribed, celebrating the city, its traditions, and the Manzanares River, an important historical landmark. The verse goes like this:
“Ay Cumaná, quien te viera y por tus calles paseara, y a San Francisco yo fuera a misa de madrugada» [Source](https://www.ventevenezuela.org/2022/09/29/ay-cumana-quien-te-viera-por-cristian-silva-potella/)
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQEXznMJApJxc9Hph1nNHP1k9b871Xy21d9NZ8jb54MmJ/image.png) María Rodríguez
Continuing on the tour, we come across murals adorned with flowers and birds, as well as the Catholic Church of Santa Inés, one of the oldest churches in Cumaná. This is where one of the most beautiful alleys in the historic district begins: El Callejón de La Purpurina. Here, the artist—who signs his work “Tony”—pays tribute to an iconic figure, María Encarnación Maiz, famous for wearing exotic, glittery makeup, hence her nickname, “La Purpurina.”
In addition to evoking this iconic figure, this alley pays homage to Cumaná’s colonial district, with its design mimicking the facades of the houses, featuring large windows adorned with colorful plants and flowers. One of the things I like most about this alley is the colorful umbrellas hanging from the ceiling; besides being decorative, they shield us from the intense sunlight.

[ESP]
Saludos estimados amigos de Worldmappin, bienvenidos a mi blog. Hoy les comparto una extraordinaria galería de fotos del arte urbano que tiene como función revitalizar los espacios del casco histórico de la ciudad de Cumaná, capital del estado Sucre, Venezuela. Además de la vistosa arquitectura colonial de la zona gracias a las coloridas casas, monumentos, calles estrechas y empedradas, para reavivar aún más a las áreas circundantes, han creado a la “Ciudad Mural”, un proyecto que recrea arte urbano a cielo abierto.
Desde que se inicia el paseo por la zona más antigua de la primogénita del continente, se observan varias escenas artísticas en todo su esplendor. Cada una de ellas representa cultura, tradiciones, identidad costeña, patrimonios, naturaleza y gastronomía oriental típica del estado Sucre. Las fachadas de las casas coloniales se convirtieron en el lienzo perfecto para las obras artísticas de la Ciudad Mural, aunque no solo fueron las casas, también negocios y hasta estacionamientos. Al converger en la plaza donde se encuentra ubicada la Basílica Menor de Santa Inés, encontramos una pintura en honor al escritor y poeta venezolano nacido en Manicuare, Cruz Salmerón Acosta.
![1772466310527.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZPTmUASxZNAp8xEEeiSGfknktS24TW9bM51oJxyvaDnA/1772466310527.jpg)
![1772466310468.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX8WhVae2a8jmoyBkaMRTvTXaLdgDAzvDWQP6Kmv5vujR/1772466310468.jpg)
Este arte urbano además de plasmar al conocido poeta del martirio, también llamado El solitario de la cima de Manicuare, muestra una escena propia de la Península de Araya, como el mar, frutos marinos y pelicanos, parte de la fauna propia de la costa. Cruz Salmerón Acosta es recordado por su poema “Azul” y en el mural además del dibujo han plasmado la primera estrofa del poema que vale la pena mencionar:
Azul de aquella cumbre tan lejana hacia la cual mi pensamiento vuela bajo la paz azul de la mañana, ¡color que tantas cosas me revela! [Fuente](https://www.poeticous.com/cruz-maria-salmeron-acosta/azul?locale=es)
Otro personaje que engalana a la Ciudad Mural es el retrato de Leonor Guerra, cuyo autor fue la artista Cubana, Ivette Dorticós, se puede observar en su firma que este arte es reciente, del año 2025. Algo que resulta fascinante de este proyecto es que siempre que se visita el casco histórico encontramos nuevas obras. Leonor de la Guerra fue una cumanesa recordada por su valentía al enfrentar a la colonia española.
![1772466310566.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbvACbKNfsp5niDDZ8zRKYX6YjX5aUY78U7Rmm11hYnXW/1772466310566.jpg)
![1777736257636.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRPZJFRJUmJeqb2GpvqA6B3JDFVWFqGdLNp1t47zNFjBE/1777736257636.jpg)
![1772466310428.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQszvbFShpt11Z8LFAc9HQJoGAzT15ggecTezU72victc/1772466310428.jpg)
La ciudad de Cumaná es una zona costera, famosa por sus playas y gastronomía marina, es considerada tierra de gracia. Es conocida como la "Primogénita del Continente Americano", al ser fundada por la colonia española, motivo por el cual contempla en sus raíces una mezcla de razas, tradiciones y cultura. Es por ello, que en la Ciudad Mural encontramos obras que conjugan y destacan elementos que confieren las raíces indígenas y africanas, paisajes marinos, fauna típica de la zona costera, tradiciones musicales folclóricas y la gastronomía, donde el plato típico principal es el pescado.
La llamada Ciudad Mural es preciosa, muy colorida, no solo por el diseño propio de la zona colonial y fachadas con arte urbano, hay muchas plantas cargadas de flores, las cuales también atraen a los turísticas con sus múltiples matices de colores. Otra de las fachadas que representan la identidad de la región, es el retrato de un niño indígena en homenaje a la raza y cultura ancestral del estado Sucre. En otra de las fachadas, el arte plasma el paisaje característico de la zona costera, gastronomía distintiva, frutos de la región y una figura de mujer que posa con un pescado sobre una tortuga de dos cabezas, esto simboliza a la estatua del indio, representativo del gentilicio Cumanés y a su vez la cálida bienvenida a los turistas cuando llegan a la ciudad. Esta estatua estuvo ubicada en una redoma donde se interceptan las Avenidas Arístides Rojas, Universidad, Arismendi y Nueva Toledo. Actualmente, la estatua no se encuentra en ese lugar, fue removida a la entrada de Cumaná, específicamente en la Avenida Universidad, Sector los Bordones.
![1772466310606.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYWi7SZTB9yXvwuVCHiDb7EWX1LEzTFzkMDTduew5MQtA/1772466310606.jpg)
![1777736257560.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQaxjudFmWX2NnLiV4A9sf37ijNr6aCnm4u1rZMugj8aT/1777736257560.jpg)
![1777736257349.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNysGfRcMji32HppcVgxRCTJaF6XcDLaSxshyPKWTFGyV/1777736257349.jpg)
![1777736257688.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSA2nUXxjASfcHMeKnEKyx1MHf6boqEkkMZLoSATc4xR6/1777736257688.jpg)
El estado Sucre y el pueblo cumanés se caracteriza por su alegría, el baile y la música, por lo que destacan muchos personajes ilustres, como Mariano Ribera, Gualberto Ibarreto y María Rodríguez, conocida como La Sirena de Cumaná. Esta última fue una importante figura de la música, muy conocida por sus bailes, motivo por el cual también era conocida como La Mariposa bailadora de Cumaná, fue cantante y cultora venezolana. En el mural donde se encuentra el retrato tributo a la Sirena de Cumaná, han plasmado algunas líneas que forman parte de la letra de la canción “Ay Cumaná”, que enaltecen a la ciudad, las tradiciones y al Río Manzanares, un importante referente histórico. La estrofa dice así:
“Ay Cumaná, quien te viera y por tus calles paseara, y a San Francisco yo fuera a misa de madrugada» [Fuente](https://www.ventevenezuela.org/2022/09/29/ay-cumana-quien-te-viera-por-cristian-silva-potella/)
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQEXznMJApJxc9Hph1nNHP1k9b871Xy21d9NZ8jb54MmJ/image.png) María Rodríguez
Continuando con el recorrido, encontramos murales cargados de flores, aves y la iglesia católica Santa Inés, uno de los templos más antiguos de Cumaná. Aquí comienza uno de los callejones más hermosos del casco histórico, El callejón de La Purpurina, en este, el autor que ha firmado con el nombre de Tony, le rinde tributo a un personaje icónico, María Encarnación Maiz, famosa por usar maquillajes exóticos y con mucho brillo, de allí su apodo, “La Purpurina”.
Este callejón además de evocar a este emblemático personaje, rinde homenaje a la zona colonial de Cumaná, simulando en su obra a las fachadas de las casas con su grandes ventanales cargados de plantas y flores coloridas. Uno de los aspectos que más me gusta de este callejón son los paraguas de colores que cuelgan sobre la parte superior del mismo, además de decorativos nos protegen de los intensos rayos solares.
![1765077278373.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP4cXNgZRgGDVfzoYkDLA849KVqnmZdkJi3ygyXTbNGcr/1765077278373.jpg)
![1765077278393.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPwpjZDf4TJC8ZXiFf7TehnwoWZMMak1ZxLfwfdJQp9Bt/1765077278393.jpg)
![1772466310706.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcSUM856Vsws48ixHMa7ttc9hZGjV6sPoyNAcvLXPx4cL/1772466310706.jpg)
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbKCwGsb5TgNN3ZjdTXxmXagZRtGGpSbB24QZkgZAjjyj/image.png)
![1765077278271.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPdkgdYqQQ6V6ceKDTnkeQBCdG5Mac6q5FXedLMFpotPH/1765077278271.jpg)
![1765077278134.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaZrdnCtm9znBj4Xpqn1ejGPNqNp1nkL3K8ZWmgkeXzXW/1765077278134.jpg)
https://images.hive.blog/DQmYSTARJw8Urk5YDMKSRND744rVT3jBwxcftjW669QcDWr/1765077278340.jpg
https://images.hive.blog/DQmW98TyVLM7v5LhXqLQfnsnkc3YQx2nMExMzmsRSmyEYAU/1765759577670.jpg
El recorrido por la ciudad mural es fascinante, hay arte por todos lados, y es que, esto es solo una muestra de este arte a cielo abierto.

![Moments in Lourdes, France.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/AKCGwSmiVaLBJuufZGiHe2s1fwWqtXUS5nUxBDdVk2ws54F39RfijcX12RzzvKa.png)
Are you Catholic? Have you ever visited a church that left you completely speechless?

In the Philippines, we have many Catholic churches—in fact, around three-fourths of the population is Catholic. That is one of the reasons why visiting Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes was part of our journey while we were in France.

This sacred place is not only known for holding Masses, but also as one of the world’s most famous pilgrimage sites. It is a place where pilgrims from different countries gather in prayer, hope, and faith. Many elderly and sick people also come here seeking peace, healing, and comfort.

As soon as we entered the gates, we immediately saw groups of pilgrims gathered around, especially near the front of the church. We arrived quite early, so the main doors still seemed closed. While waiting, we walked around the area first—and honestly, it felt less like a church and more like a grand castle.

The entire sanctuary is massive, with breathtaking architecture and intricate details everywhere. Even the bridge leading up to the entrance felt magical, like walking toward a royal castle from a fairytale.

Once inside, we saw statues and images of famous saints from around the world, although photography was no longer allowed inside the basilicas. Most of my photos were therefore taken outside. But inside—it was truly beyond words. The beauty, history, and atmosphere were simply incredible.

Within the sanctuary, you can find the Basilica of the Immaculate Conception, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary, and the underground Basilica of Saint Pius X.

The entire place is unbelievably vast. What amazed me the most was the underground basilica—you simply cannot imagine how such a huge underground structure could have been built. Standing there made me feel both small and deeply amazed at the same time.

![2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/AJehXNeaFwByjnF4HsyvTbGbtHMZgpQzZM8YaN8PQFAM1apxuro1DHYuBh3qt53.png)

![4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/AKNKMbhrZS6Lu5dKgEUyfEDPsckku2iJ7VG6YB2HXr7XAGAd16N9LBjzR3YQKiT.png)
As we walked toward the left side of the sanctuary, we saw a fast-flowing river running between the church grounds and another building, which I believe was a place where sick pilgrims and elderly visitors could stay during their pilgrimage and healing journey. A bridge connected the sanctuary to the building, adding even more charm to the peaceful surroundings.

The river flowed all the way from the entrance area of Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes, where we also caught sight of the magnificent Château Fort de Lourdes. 

![3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/AK3fanV56HMFV4Cem11QgPV8uzxAniqgEHxLmpbrTkAT1DW46YJwWoTpteeH95k.png)
Here, I took some photos of the souvenir shops just outside the sanctuary. There were also many restaurants and hotels nearby, making the area feel lively and welcoming for pilgrims and visitors.

As for souvenirs, we bought a few magnets from Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes to display on our fridge, along with a cross for our wall and a few other keepsakes.

One thing that really caught my attention was how almost every shop sold large bottles, gallons, and different kinds of containers for carrying holy water home. Many pilgrims bring holy water back with them as a symbol of faith, hope, and healing.

Thankfully, we already had a large empty bottle with us, so we didn’t need to buy one. To be honest, the containers sold there were quite expensive.

![20250702_115324[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/242Y5pjBahj777FizgBStZjNbeSTWRZ9uJx8PAmN29YtLfEyyAJjhnnLJkj5wv5a5ipbT.jpg)

![20250702_142956[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/241tZCszytcZFGMoGRzBXCwfh1SZs3YxSbm4DakXWBa5HseYESW5S9Y3sjnoTr6ebWzfA.jpg)
Keep in mind that the water flowing throughout the basilica grounds is considered holy water. Around the sanctuary, there are fountains, faucets, and small flowing canals where pilgrims can wash their faces, drink the water, or collect it to bring home. Of course, I did the same—I refilled our empty bottle so I could take some holy water back home to Germany. ✨🙏🏻

This sacred place is known as the site of the apparitions of the Virgin Mary to Bernadette Soubirous, where a “miraculous” spring is said to have emerged. “Massabielle” means “old rock” in the Gascon language. Every day, thousands of pilgrims pass through the grotto to touch the damp stone walls beneath the statue of the Virgin Mary, which was installed in 1864. Over time, the rock walls have become smooth from the countless hands of pilgrims, showing the deep faith and devotion connected to Lourdes.

It was the Virgin herself, according to tradition, who told Bernadette about the healing and spiritual benefits of the clear and pure spring water. Today, visitors can collect the water from taps installed near the grotto.

Processions are also regularly held within the sanctuary, allowing pilgrims to offer prayers and wishes. Carrying blessed candles, they walk together in remembrance of Bernadette Soubirous and her extraordinary story.
We felt truly fortunate to attend the Mass at the grotto before the procession began. After the Mass, people gathered and formed a long line leading toward the grotto, where pilgrims gently touched the rocks believed to bring healing, protection, and blessings for their families.

Of course, we also joined the line and took part in this meaningful experience.

![20250702_114607[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/EpviSWLuGgneGGYfxDgDGiXEZsp9yWx6FNgSMwwjKdYvudJdDbEY7W8J4tJtVfnKiek.jpg)

![20250702_114940[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/244xwuacFZEsg8q7vKpJcp4xNrqkHDPbinqJA5FyEZP8RcNGWpMboaXkBy5s2i8w9TDU8.jpg)

The river flowed all the way from the entrance area of Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes, where we also caught sight of the magnificent Château Fort de Lourdes.
Even from a distance, the castle looked absolutely incredible. It amazed me how these two historic and breathtaking landmarks stood so close to each other.

Perched high on a rocky hill, the castle almost felt as if it was watching over the entire town. Sadly, we didn’t have enough time to visit it during this trip, but perhaps we can add it to our list for the next visit to Lourdes.

![20250702_115545[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/23x16wSZ7aRoscJs5GyoMX7waMfwscPsrBgvY4gDFSymKBMwiAj2cysexrtuSuVgikG32.jpg)

![IMG-20250702-WA0018[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/245wKxGZuuruVUStBtHAezF5bzpkZXwNhwgRk2oERUbiKY2wWrrVrtHeXudreZ9acRTm5.jpg)

![IMG-20250702-WA0008[1].jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macaroth90/EnaZGZDSnLEsbyXq8fwJBJK1AuStdkwvPE12DufLB1wcSGVt73adALyAHx9fdMLuPQR.jpg)
